title: Interdisciplinary Care and Systemic Therapy in von Hippel–Lindau Disease – A Prospective Single-Center Observational Study on the Clinical Use of Belzutifan at Ulm University Hospital
summary:
Study Overview
This study at Ulm University Hospital focuses on people with von Hippel–Lindau disease (VHL).
It has two main parts:
•	Understanding VHL patients (their symptoms, tumors, and overall health)
•	Observing a new treatment, Belzutifan, in real-life use
This is a non-interventional (observational) study, meaning:
•	No extra risky procedures
•	Care is the same as standard treatment
About the Treatment (Belzutifan)
Some patients will receive Belzutifan if they:
•	Have active tumors or symptoms affecting daily life
Others may:
•	Be monitored (“watch and wait”)
•	Receive local treatments (e.g., surgery or radiotherapy)
What the Study Wants to Find Out
Researchers aim to understand:
•	How well Belzutifan works (tumor shrinkage, symptom relief)
•	Whether it improves:
o	Daily functioning
o	Pain
o	Neurological symptoms
o	Kidney function
•	What side effects occur and how often
•	How safe and tolerable the treatment is in real life
What Participation Involves
Regular Check-ups
Patients will have routine tests such as:
•	Blood tests (including kidney and liver function)
•	Oxygen levels
•	MRI scans (every 2–3 months)
•	Physical and neurological exams
During Treatment
•	Medication taken once daily
•	Regular monitoring:
o	Every 2 weeks at first, then monthly
•	Dose may be reduced if side effects occur
Eye Examinations
Because VHL can affect the eyes:
•	Regular eye exams every 3–6 months
•	Tests include vision checks and retinal imaging
Additional Assessments
Every few months, patients may also complete:
•	Questionnaires on quality of life, mood, and stress
•	Simple memory and thinking tests
•	Pain ratings
How Patients Are Selected
You may be included if you:
•	Are 18 years or older
•	Have confirmed or suspected VHL
•	Give written consent
You cannot participate if:
•	You cannot attend visits
•	MRI is not possible (e.g., certain implants, severe claustrophobia)
Data & Safety
•	Patient data is pseudonymized (your identity is protected)
•	No additional risks beyond normal care
•	Participation is voluntary and does not affect your treatment
Study Size
•	About 30 patients are expected to take part
Key Takeaway
This study helps doctors better understand:
•	How VHL behaves over time
•	How well Belzutifan works in everyday practice
•	How to improve treatment and patient quality of life

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Genetically confirmed diagnosis of von Hippel–Lindau (VHL) disease or presence of tumors characteristic of the syndrome (with or without a positive family history of VHL)
•	Written informed consent for study participation provided by the patient
Exclusion criteria:
•	Inability to adequately understand the patient information
•	Inability to attend study visits
•	Contraindications to MRI
